newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine and Russia re-unite electricity grids.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine and Russia re-unite electricity grids.

text.p: Ukraine has been plugged back into the Russian electricity grid after a two-year separation, which could improve supplies and boost exports, energy officials said on Wednesday.

"The power grids of Ukraine and Russia were unified on Tuesday," Oksana Liven, spokeswoman for the Energy and Electricification Ministry, said. "It will make our grid more stable, especially its frequency."
Ukraine and Russia were part of a single electrical grid until 1995, when Moscow disconnected Kiev after accusing it of helping itself to too much electricity.
Ukraine's portion of the network continued to function independently, but it is grossly inefficient and technologically inferior.
The tying together of the two grids means Kiev may be able to import and possibly export more Russian electricity, as well as use its own supplies more efficiently.

"The Ukrainian electrical system will work better and more reliably," Olexander Voyevoda, Ukraine's chief electrical dispatcher, said by telephone. "Russia has a stable frequency which corresponds to Western standards."
He said the united grid also meant three Ukrainian regions -- Kharkiv, Poltava and Sumy, all in the northeast -- would receive steady supplies again.
He said Russia had a central dispatching centre regulating supplies, adding, "Ukraine has no such thing, so now we can rely on Russia's base."
Ukraine benefits from the move since its nuclear reactors often undergo maintenance or stoppages.
Its 41 thermal, five nuclear and six hydrostations produced 181 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity last year compared to 300 billion in 1990, a year before the demise of the Soviet Union.
Local news agencies reported reactor number one at the Zaporizhya nuclear station in eastern Ukraine had been switched off due to minor technical problems.
Ukraine has been suffering from an electricity shortage for several years, with some regions switched off for several hours a day in past years, even during the winter.
Ukraine's grid frequency is between 49.35 to 49.55 megahertz, under the 50 megahertz standard.
Kiev-based Pravex has a deal to import 3.6 billion kilowatt hours of Russian electricity a year.

Last week, Ukrainian government officials announced plans to boost electricity exports to Hungary, Slovakia and Poland to 15-16 billion kilowatt hours a year after 2000 from current levels of 4.5 billion.
Ukraine's exports are from the Burshtynska thermal station in the west. The station is separate from the national grid and works on a stable frequency.
